name: Generic UVC Webcam
description: Typical USB UVC camera defaults with common V4L2 controls

meta.notes: Attach this model to a Webcam part to push reasonable defaults; per-device overrides still apply
meta.geometryNote: defaults are the OPERATIONAL geometry this fleet streams at, not the sensor maximum (see maxResolution). The live setting is owned by scripts/mjpg-launcher.sh, overridable per node via /etc/default/monsterbox-cam. These defaults only seed a new part; nothing here configures the camera. Read mjpgStreamer.activeGeometry from the webcam health endpoint for what is actually streaming.

name: Arducam B0205 Wide-Angle USB Camera
description: Arducam 1080p 200-degree wide-angle USB camera with infrared night vision, auto-focus, f/1.6 aperture, 1/2.7-inch CMOS sensor

meta.notes: Compact 200-degree fisheye lens with IR night vision. IR switching is hardware-automatic (ambient light sensor). Night Mode preset optimizes V4L2 controls for IR viewing.
meta.geometryNote: defaults are the OPERATIONAL geometry this fleet streams at, not the sensor maximum (see maxResolution). The live setting is owned by scripts/mjpg-launcher.sh, overridable per node via /etc/default/monsterbox-cam. These defaults only seed a new part; nothing here configures the camera. Read mjpgStreamer.activeGeometry from the webcam health endpoint for what is actually streaming.

name: SONix Streaming Camera (USB UVC)
description: USB UVC camera built on a SONix streaming controller. Enumerates as a composite device - one UVC video interface plus a UAC capture stream - so the host sees both a camera and a microphone from the same plug.

meta.notes: USB signature read from a live device on a MonsterNet node via /sys/bus/usb/devices. It identifies the MODEL, not the individual unit, so an identical replacement camera still matches. Many rebadged wide-angle USB cameras ship this same controller - read a match as 'same camera model', not 'same retail SKU'. controlsSchema is left empty on purpose: the V4L2 control ranges for this unit have not been measured, and inventing them would push wrong defaults at the device.
